To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the potential for financial savings through energy conservation is vast, that there are significant barriers to the development of energy conservation programs at the local level and that there is little meaningful technical assistance available to local governments.

(a) the federal government has been a major source of technical assistance to state and local governments in energy conservation, but this assistance has declined since 1980 and is likely to decline in the future; (b) state governments have not been active in energy conservation, and their technical assistance to local governments has been limited and declining; (c) local governments have been relatively inactive and have been slow to develop energy conservation programs, but their energy conservation activities have increased in recent years; (d

the potential for financial and physical savings by local government energy conservation programs is vast, yet there are very few local energy conservation programs and the programs that do exist are poorly developed.

the role that local government can play in energy conservation, particularly in the area of energy efficiency in the built environment.

the research on local government energy conservation programs is in its infancy and is a promising area for future research.

the energy crisis is here to stay.

the local governments are not the primary actors in the energy field, and they are not the ones who have the most influence over energy policy.
